role: FastAPI microservice wrapping OpenCV+YOLO perception pipeline as HTTP endpoints for NestJS backend
detail: A thin HTTP wrapper around Layer 2 perception stack (YOLO object detection, MediaPipe face detection, VLM captioning). Exposes 8 endpoints: /perception/health (model status), /perception/detect (one-shot YOLO on JPEG), /perception/detect-annotated (detection + annotated JPEG), /perception/crop-face (crop + EfficientNet-B0 embedding), /perception/caption (VLM scene description), /perception/status (pipeline metrics), /perception/stream (annotated MJPEG), /perception/stream/raw (unannotated MJPEG). All state stored in _AppState singleton to avoid global scope. Lazy-initializes VLM, embedding extractor, and face detector on first use. Tracker (IoUTracker) maintains persistent object IDs across frames. Uses asyncio.Lock for atomic frame_sequence increment and threading.Lock for thread-safe lazy-init of ONNX extractor and VLM. NestJS owns all Neo4j graph writes via null PersistenceCheck stub. Runs on port 8430.
gotchas: Threading complexity: _embedding_init_lock and _vlm_init_lock protect lazy-init race conditions in executor threads; double-checked locking patterns used. Frame sequence must be atomic across async requests (asyncio.Lock protects increment-and-read). Camera device can be unavailable (startup non-fatal, service starts with model_loaded=False); endpoints return 503 if model not loaded. VLM model lazy-loaded on first caption request (multi-GB download). Face landmark mask applied only if 10+ landmarks provided. No segmentation mask handling if mask_polygon has <3 points. Global _embedding_init_failed flag prevents repeated init attempts. SIGTERM handler only registered on non-Windows (add_signal_handler not supported). No actual graph persistence---NestJS side-channel; this service is read-only detector.
